title: Rapid runbook: runtime sprint triage
content:
Goal for today: clear the highest-risk p99 regressions and leave an actionable runbook for on-call. Quick hits first, deep dives later.

Morning snapshot:
- Observed: p99 token latency spikes in region-us-west over last 6h, correlated with spikes in small-control-model traffic.
- Hypothesis A: KV-cache eviction storm when sequences align with autoscaler bursts -> transient cache miss cascade.
- Hypothesis B: Micro-batching scheduler sometimes forms very large batches for short sequences -> CPU mutex contention during kernel dispatch.

Triage steps performed:
1) Pulled traces for route /v1/generate (span ids: clipped) and filtered by host pool; saw 3x increase in cache-miss ratio during spikes.
2) Matched times with autoscaler events (autoscale logs show 2x new workers at t=02:14).
3) Reproduced locally (small sim harness) by running synthetic burst pattern: pattern = 30 rps for 90s then 5 rps. Repro reproducible ~2/3 runs.

Immediate mitigations (do these now)
- [ ] Disable aggressive prefix-caching TTL override in config for region-us-west (config key: runtime.cache.prefix_ttl_override). Rollback plan: re-enable after 1h if no regression. Owner: Arjun.
- [ ] Add temporary rate-smoothing (leaky bucket) at edge for control-model route to smooth bursts. Owner: Mina.

Perf TODOs (prioritized)
- Short term: introduce sampling of KV-cache eviction events and emit metric evict_burst_count per-minute (metric name: runtime.kv.evict_burst). Low risk, high signal. Estimated 2-3h.
- Mid term: tweak batcher backpressure to cap max-batch-window for sequences < 64 tokens (config rights: batcher.max_window_ms_small_seq). Owner: me (Kiyoko).
- Long term: prototype async eviction handler to avoid blocking main scheduler. Spike task -> infra/bench next sprint.

Kernel notes / commands used
- Repro harness: tools/sim/mini_burst.py --rps 30 --duration 90 --seq-len-dist small --warmup 60
- Trace extraction: go run tools/tracegrep/main.go --span-prefix=runtime/kv --start=2025-02-14T01:30:00Z --end=2025-02-14T03:00:00Z > traces.txt
- Kernel logs: nvprof snapshots around suspected window, saved to /tmp/nvprof-usw-0214.tar.gz

Open questions / hypotheses to validate
- Is eviction storm caused by many small entries or a few large ones? (quick inspect: sample 100 evicted keys, size histogram)
- Does new worker join trigger synchronous rebalancing that forces cache flush? (check join-handler codepath in cluster-manager)
- Are there any client-side retries amplifying bursts? (look into gateway logs for 429->retry loops)

Next steps / handoff 
- Pair with Arjun at 11:00 PST to flip TTL override and monitor for 30m. Alert criteria: p99 > baseline + 20% for two consecutive 5-min windows.
- If mitigation fails, escalate to SRE (pager: oncall-sre) and prepare plan B: route control-model to lower-priority worker pool.
- Document final mitigations and lessons in Confluence page linked above.

Notes to self: keep the reproducer deterministic—add jitter control flag. Capture full kernel-stacktrace next run (set KERNEL_DEBUG=1). Save perf artifacts in drive folder: shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/temp/perf-runs-2025-02-14.

End-of-day checklist:
- [ ] Confirm metric emitted and dashboard tile created for evict_burst_count.
- [ ] Close INFR-3127 with root cause hypothesis and attach traces.
- [ ] Write a short postmortem if spikes persisted after mitigations.

Random thoughts / heuristics:
- When autoscaler adds workers quickly, prefer passive warming (keep old cache entries sticky) rather than eager rekeying.
- Small-control traffic often behaves like a metronome; smoothing at edge is usually lowest-risk fix.

If I get blocked: ping @arjun on slack and drop the raw trace tarball in #runtime-debug.
